building.quote: Chapter 5 of the Code of Ordinances of the City of Columbia regulates buildings within the city limits. The City of Columbia adopts building codes generally every two years. The following codes are in effect for South Carolina: 2021 International Building Code with SC modifications [...] 2021 International Plumbing Code with SC modifications [...] ICC A117.1-2026 Standard for Accessible and Usable Buildings and Facilities. Please note, as of September 18, 2026, City of Columbia has been informed that the 2026 version of ICC A117.1 has been made available for use. Per SC State Law, adoption and enforcement is mandatory upon publication for the accessibility code. Please ensure your project is in compliance with the newly published edition. [...] The City will be adopting the 2024 Code Edition effective 1 January 2027. Any request for permit submitted to the City after December 31, 2026, will have to follow the 2024 Building Code Editions.

building.local_amendments_note: None found. State law lets a city change the technical codes only with the Building Codes Council's approval. The Council's 2021 Modification Index and 2024 Final Modification Index list no modification requested by or for Columbia, and the Council's adoption page lists one pending local request (Greenville County, Appendix BE). Chapter 5 of the Columbia Code of Ordinances (Municode) could not be opened by automated access, so the city's own adopting sections, and which administrative provisions it adopted, were not read.

scheduled_change.what: 2024 South Carolina Building Code and 2024 South Carolina Plumbing Code (2024 International codes with SC modifications) replace the 2021 editions. City wording: "The City will be adopting the 2024 Code Edition effective 1 January 2027. Any request for permit submitted to the City after December 31, 2026, will have to follow the 2024 Building Code Editions." Per the state pack, the office, restaurant and school toilet counts, the 50/50 split, rounding, the separate-rooms exceptions and the HDPE fire test read the same in the 2024 editions.

fixtures.city_amends_note: Columbia enforces the state's fixture table unchanged. South Carolina cities may not modify the building codes without the Building Codes Council's approval ("Building code modifications that have not been approved by the Council are invalid and cannot be adopted, employed or enforced by municipalities and counties"), and neither Council modification index (2021, 2024) lists a Columbia modification. The only Chapter 29 modifications are statewide: IPC 2021-05 (bottle filling station column), the 2022 emergency deletion of the all-gender multi-user exceptions, and their continuation as IBC 2024 11 and 12. The city's commercial upfit checklist asks for the "Plumbing fixture count" and "Occupancy loads" in the code design data on the plans, with no city table of its own. Not read: Chapter 5 of the Columbia Code of Ordinances.
fixtures.worked_examples_note: Not redone: the state pack's twelve examples apply (office 1/1, 2/2, 3/3, 5/5; restaurant 1/1, 1/1, 2/2, 3/3; school 1/1, 1/1, 2/2, 4/4 at 50, 100, 200 and 400 occupants).

permit.exempt_list_quote: [City of Columbia, Commercial & Multi-family Projects] All regulated work performed in the City of Columbia must have a permit. Two types of permits can be issued depending on the type of work being performed; either a Building Permit or a Building Trade Permit. A Building Trade Permit includes work such as electrical, mechanical, plumbing, and gas that typically does not require the review of Zoning, the Plans Examiner, Engineering or other agency outside of Permitting including minor commercial up-fits that do not require plan review. [...] NOTE: Painting, flooring, and other cosmetic work does not require a building permit; see the International Building Code Section 105.2 for exceptions. [2021 South Carolina Building Code, read on UpCodes] [A] 105.1 Required. Any owner or owner's authorized agent who intends to construct, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish or change the occupancy of a building or structure [...] shall first make application to the building official and obtain the required permit. [A] 105.2 Work Exempt From Permit. Exemptions from permit requirements of this code shall not be deemed to grant authorization for any work to be done in any manner in violation of the provisions of this code or any other laws or ordinances of this jurisdiction. Permits shall not be required for the following: Building: One-story detached accessory structures [...] Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. [...] Nonfixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches (1753 mm) in height.
permit.partitions_named_note: Toilet partitions are not named, on the city's page or in Section 105.2. The only partitions on the list are "nonfixed and movable" ones not over 5 feet 9 inches; toilet partitions are fixed to the floor, wall or ceiling. Whether a like-for-like replacement is "cosmetic work" or "similar finish work" is not stated. In South Carolina the administrative chapter of the building code applies only where the city adopts it by ordinance; the city's page points to Section 105.2, but Chapter 5 of the city code, which would show the adoption and any local change to the list, could not be opened. The list was read on UpCodes (secondary).

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Columbia, SC job sites. Price your restroom, pick a material for Midlands humidity and see the local rules.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Columbia state offices, university buildings, hospitals and schools, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** South Carolina's building rules, which Columbia enforces without changes of its own, set the number of toilets by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **South Carolina extras:** the state's access standard asks for more than the federal one in a few places. In the edition used until September 2026, the accessible stall needs a vertical grab bar on the side wall as well as the horizontal bars, and the gap under its partitions must be 12 inches high where the federal rule asks for 9. A room with six or more toilets and urinals also needs a narrower stall with grab bars on both sides, as under federal law. Columbia says a newer edition, published in September 2026, now applies to projects, so confirm the stall details with the City's commercial plan review (803-545-3427).
extra_rule_bullets: - **New rules on January 1, 2027:** Columbia moves to the next edition of South Carolina's building and plumbing rules on that date. A permit request submitted to the City after December 31, 2026 has to follow the new edition. The toilet counts in the table below, the rule that every toilet needs its own stall with a door and the fire test for solid plastic are the same in the new edition.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Columbia requires a permit for all regulated work. The City says painting, flooring and other cosmetic work doesn't need a building permit and points to the building rules' list of exempt work. That list covers painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, countertops and similar finish work, and movable partitions no taller than 5 feet 9 inches. It doesn't name toilet partitions fixed to the floor or wall, so ask the City of Columbia Development Center (803-545-3483) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Columbia Development Center
page.install_rule: Installers need a City of Columbia business license and must show their credentials to the building official before a permit is issued. With a commercial permit application the City asks for a copy of the contractor's state license, the current city business license and the signed contract. South Carolina requires a state contractor license when a commercial project's total construction cost is over $10,000. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Columbia the contractor needs a city business license, and a state contractor license when the project's total cost is over $10,000.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** South Carolina has no state wage law for public construction, so a set wage applies only on federally funded jobs, under the federal Davis-Bacon Act. For a carpenter on building work in Richland County that is $16.32 an hour plus $3.83 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 8% in Columbia: 6% state, 1% Richland County local option tax and 1% Richland County transportation tax. The part of Columbia in Lexington County is taxed at 7%.
page.buyers_extra: - **State offices, university buildings and hospitals:** phenolic or stainless steel where restrooms are cleaned many times a day, HDPE where heavy traffic is hard on stalls.

After January 1, 2027: update the code names in the Sources list to the 2024 editions and recheck the exempt-work list and the counts in the 2024 South Carolina codes.

The federal carpenter rate for Richland County ($16.32 plus $3.83) comes from a 2011 wage survey and is below the area's median carpenter wage on the same page ($23.11). It applies only to federally funded building work; determinations are reissued each January, so recheck in early 2027.

Sales tax: the 8% rate is for addresses in Richland County, downtown included. Columbia addresses in Lexington County are at 7%. The Department of Revenue lists no rate change for Richland County; recheck its Local Sales Taxes page before launch.
